A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GraphVid study. All 34 pages, including Appendices A–G and the subsequent prompt templates, are readable. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, generated-video examples, and a human preference study involving 60 participants and 10 scenarios (Section 5; Appendices C–F).

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, generated-video examples, and 60-participant preference study (Section 5; Appendices C–F).

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical graph construction, edge-aware GINE message passing, graph-to-token adaptation, frozen video backbone, LoRA conditioning, and flow-matching objective. The inference and training prompt templates also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GraphVid-Bench training sources and evaluate the same interaction-centric MoveBench, multi-object MoveBench, and DAVIS subsets. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment. Tables 2, 3, and 8 retain their respective selections of Wan-Move, Motion-I2V, Tora, MagicMotion, WISA, and FlashMotion; Appendix D retains the same human-study comparators.

E3.justification: Filtering, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, training settings, ablation configurations, and human-study procedures are identical. Both retain 512×288 evaluation resolution, 81 frames at 16 FPS, and the 60-participant, 10-scenario study.

E4.justification: Both retain the backbone, graph-capacity, conditioning-modality, and LoRA-rank ablations (Tables 4–7), node-only training ablation (Table 9), qualitative comparisons, and small-symbol grounding failure analysis (Appendices E–F).

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Dataset summary statistics in Table 1 and human-preference aggregation in Appendix D remain identical.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match. For example, GraphVid's Table 2 results remain FID 17.02, FVD 99.42, PSNR 15.98, SSIM 0.61, and EPE 2.9. Appendix benchmark, ablation, and preference results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The interaction-graph definitions, message-passing equation (1), and flow-matching equation (2) are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about interactive graph control, edge-aware reasoning, GraphVid-Bench, generation quality, and computational and data efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of relational conditioning, attention dilution, backbone transfer, and efficiency are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same small-symbol grounding limitation, and Appendix G retains the same broader-impact discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation dimensions, hyperparameters, hardware, training duration, preprocessing instructions, sampling details, project link, and prompt templates are identical (Section 5.1, Appendices A–B, and pages 29–34).

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 60 reference entries are unchanged. Positioning relative to trajectory control, physics-aware generation, and earlier graph-based generation remains identical.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 23 July 2026 to v2 dated 25 August 2026, and PDF author metadata corrects name spellings. Printed authors, paper prose, headings, and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: Only the first-page marginal arXiv stamp changes formatting and position. Figures 1–12, Tables 1–9, and the body layout remain unchanged; rendered pages 2–34 are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 updates the arXiv stamp and corrects author metadata while retaining identical scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and appendices. These administrative adjustments do not meaningfully improve or weaken the paper's overall quality.
